title: Host and none networks
idea: `--network host` makes a container share the host's network directly. `--network none` gives it no network at all except loopback, the container's own `localhost`.
points: `--network host` skips network isolation: the container uses the host's own network.
The container has no IP of its own; its port 3000 is the host's.
`-p` is ignored in host mode, and two servers cannot share one port.
`--network none` creates only a loopback device; nothing else can connect in or out.

walk.text: Host mode: the API's port 3000 is the host's port 3000. No `-p`.
Request it through the host's own `localhost`.
None mode: list the container's network interfaces. Only loopback (`lo`) appears.

pitfalls: Docker Desktop 4.34+ needs "Enable host networking" turned on in Settings first.
Do not add `-p` in host mode; Docker ignores it.
Host mode removes network isolation; any port your app opens is open on the host.

quiz.q: An app listens on port 3000 in a container started with `--network host`. How do you reach it?
options: At the host's port 3000; no `-p` needed
You cannot; the container has no IP
quiz.why: Host mode shares the host's network, so the app's port is the host's port. `-p` is ignored.

takeaway: `host` shares the host's network, `none` removes the network, `bridge` is the default.
